title: Folding Interrupted: Defective Folding of Mutant Gβ5 by the CCT Chaperone Complex
content: Protein folding is an essential step in maintaining protein homeostasis. While many proteins can fold spontaneously, others with complex structures require the assistance of chaperones to adopt their native states [1]. The Chaperonin Containing Tailless polypeptide-1 (CCT) is a chaperone estimated to fold ∼10% of cytosolic proteins [2]. One major class of proteins that CCT folds are β-propeller containing proteins [3], including the G protein β5 subunit (Gβ5), which forms dimers with Regulator of G protein Signaling (RGS) proteins to catalyze GTP hydrolysis on G protein α subunits (Gα) and set the duration of G protein coupled receptor (GPCR) signaling cascades. These signaling cascades are reliant on correctly folded Gβ proteins, and missense mutations of Gβ5 are associated with neuro-developmental disorders. These disorders include Language Delay and ADHD/Cognitive Impairment with or without cardiac arrhythmia (LADCI) and Intellectual Development Disorder with Cardiac Arrhythmia (IDDCA) [5-6]. Several of these mutations could interfere with Gβ5 folding; however, the molecular basis of how these mutations might disrupt folding are unknown [5-7].
